turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes, Hale. My son found out he had a zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
You asked for this meeting, so skip the pleasantries. Was Owen heard before that zero went into the gradebook?
How do I wrap up this meeting?
You answer my question, and then I'm out of your classroom. Who entered the zero, and did anyone talk to Owen first?
What happens after we finish? Do I get a summary?
You'll get an email from me tonight, and it goes to the principal too. If you want a summary, write it yourself. Right now the zero comes off, and I still don't have an answer on who decided it.
